hypothesis: Amortize the cost identified in the first end-to-end service pilot. Fit a shared key-space read basis for each recurrent value head once, install it at both endpoints, then transmit only coefficients of the current state change on those directions. The sender receives the updated facts and does not see the two downstream questions. A fair basis-independent comparison includes one-bit and two-bit matrix transmission, shared random directions, an equally sized basis fitted to training matrix differences, sending no recurrent correction, dense state, and exact text-patch replay. The attention and convolution corrections are carried in every cache policy.
task: Split public bAbI and MQuAKE development cases by SHA-256('shared-doc-v1/'+source+'/'+id). Take six per task for fitting and the next six per task for evaluation. All 24 were available to earlier development; no claim of a fresh public-test cohort. Each of the 12 evaluation documents is edited before a new user query. Both the changed and stable question are distinct future continuations of the same document cache and are decoded freely. One sender update per document, then two receiver questions. Fitters get old and updated public facts, generic template boundary markers only and no answer strings or evaluation queries.
candidate: Four orthonormal key-space directions per head fit by PCA over unit-length transported queries observed at the first four template delimiter tokens across fitting documents. Serialize and install float16 basis values. For each update transmit only four float16 coefficients per value dimension. Receiver applies the matching factors to its old float32 matrix. Both endpoint models and all other banks are fixed. Fit an alternative basis from leading right singular vectors of fitting update matrices; use the same transmitted coefficients and storage. A deterministic isotropic basis is the third parameter-matched control.
comparators: Same receiver old snapshots at 32-token boundaries. Include (i) UTF-8 splice with full/prefix-reused prefill, (ii) dense KV-suffix plus conv plus full recurrent state, (iii) no matrix, (iv) per-row 1-bit residual with two FP16 centroids, (v) per-row 2-bit affine residual with fp16 endpoints, (vi) matched random basis, (vii) matched offline SVD basis. All receiver caches are reconstructed explicitly. Logical FP16 basis installation is charged once per receiver and its size and fit cost are separately disclosed. Local GPU moves use MLX operations for both candidate and quantized controls.
timing: Measure donor construction, encoding, actual framed socket send at a paced 1 Gbit/s, receiver reconstruction, then both questions. The cap is emulated on a local socket, not an internet measurement. Rotate methods across documents. Report elapsed mean and per-document paired results, bytes, and both warm and cold sender. For one cold client, sender prefill duplicates receiver replay. Warm donor or broadcast are separate serving conditions. Count fit time and one-time receiver basis bytes separately and compute honest deployment break-even. No net cold single-client advantage assumed.
gate: Before a larger transfer experiment require all 24 full-donor answer token sequences, both dataset accuracy counts preserved, and at least two more exact sequences than no-matrix. For a savings claim require >=20% lower complete warm-donor service (including both unknown questions) against the fastest equal-quality practical control. Also publish ready-to-continue times explicitly, the uncached cold result, and matched random/SVD comparisons. If only update-ready latency improves, or only a text baseline is beaten, report a narrower result and leave new cases sealed. Deployment and generic activation-aware compression have precedents; do not claim novelty without an independent comparative advantage.
budget: Up to 15 minutes of local calibration and 25 minutes of local evaluation, one engineering repair per phase. No paid GPU startup until the case for a bigger test is established; GPU permission is available within existing budgets.
